key_insight: An ultralow-loss silicon nitride photonic chip integrates photon-pair sources, qubit fusion, and state analysis to push discrete-variable quantum processing beyond loss-limited scaling barriers.
engineering_relevance: The work shows a CMOS-compatible, wafer-scale photonic platform that can fabricate and operate larger quantum circuits with substantially improved yield and performance.
method: Monolithic Si3N4 integrated photonic circuit with narrowband photon-pair sources.
On-chip fusion of two EPR pairs to generate four-photon GHZ states.
Reconfigurable interferometers for state analysis on the same chip.
evidence_signal: The platform achieved EPR-state fidelity of 0.9875(3), heralded Hong-Ou-Mandel visibility of 0.990(6), and four-photon GHZ-state fidelity of 0.943(8) with a 27 Hz fourfold count rate.
watch_item: Although losses are greatly reduced, system performance still depends on precise fabrication, interferometric stability, and scalable integration of sources and routing at larger circuit depths.
paper_title: An ultralow-loss integrated photonic platform for discrete-variable quantum information processing
